full_judgment: 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that the petitioner as plain-till instituted a suit for specific performance of contract in respect of 183/4 decimals of land in the court of the Assistant Judge, Shariatpur sadar (Chikandi) being Title Suit No. 21 of 1994, alleging, inter alia that the suit land measuring 183/4 decimals along with other lands recorded in S.A. Plot No. 161. 162 and 163 under S.A. Khatian Nos. 47. 82 and 120 of Mouza No. 80 Dhanuka, P.S. palong belonged to Nilkrishna pal and others. While being the rightful owner in possession of the suit property Nilkrishna intended to sell his share to the plaintiff and eventually on 27.6.91entered into an agreement to sell the land to him at a consideration of Tk. 10.000/- only and in pursuance of the said agreement Nilkrishna Pal duly executed a bainapatra in favour of plaintiff on receipt of Tk. 9,500/- as earnest money in part performance of the contract. It was stipulated between in parties that Nilkrishna Pal would soon execute and register a sale deed in favour of the plain-tiff on receipt of the balance of the consideration money. It was contended that. the petitioner in due course offered the balance of the consideration money to Nilkrishna Pal who consumed time on some plea or the other and eventually refused to execute and register the promised kabala on 3rd Paush. 1400 B.S and hence the Suit.
